top_news.summary: In a major cross-border enforcement breakthrough that swiftly triggered retaliatory unrest on the ground, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has announced the capture of Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, one of its Ten Most Wanted fugitives, following a Mexican military operation backed by US assistance. The arrest prompted the US State Department to issue an urgent security alert for American citizens across parts of Mexico's Sinaloa state after overnight armed clashes, road blockades and vehicle fires erupted in its wake. Meza-Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro", faces accusations of heading a Sinaloa Cartel network that smuggled lethal narcotics, including fentanyl, into American communities. Confirming the apprehension on November 21, FBI Director Kash Patel noted that Mexican forces had detained the alleged cartel boss with US backing, highlighting it as the 11th arrest of an FBI Ten Most Wanted fugitive under the Trump administration. "Another FBI Ten Most Wanted fugitive is off the board. Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," has been captured by Mexican forces with U.S. assistance," Patel said in a statement, thanking law enforcement counterparts in Mexico as well as the US agencies involved in the operation. According to the US Department of Justice, Meza-Flores was apprehended on November 20 in Guasave, located in Mexico's Sinaloa state, following an investigation led by the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF). The operation also resulted in the capture of a second alleged cartel figure, German Rolando Galvez Meza, known as "El Serafin". Praising the HSTF and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) for tracking down Meza-Flores and aiding the operation, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin underscored the reach of the joint effort. "The arrest of Chapo Isidro demonstrates the outstanding strength and reach of the Homeland Security Task Force," Mullin said in the Justice Department statement. He noted that Meza-Flores's syndicate was accused of pouring lethal narcotics into American neighbourhoods and subjecting communities to extreme violence. "This operation sends an unmistakable message, cartel leaders cannot hide behind borders, money, or brutality," Mullin said, adding that the task force will press ahead with efforts to break up criminal and terrorist networks, bring their leaders to justice and safeguard Americans. The probe brought together the FBI's Washington and San Diego field offices, HSI San Diego, the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and the US Marshals Service, according to the Justice Department. As news of Meza-Flores's capture reverberated across Sinaloa, the US Consulate General in Hermosillo released a notice on November 21 stating that it was tracking reports of active security operations, armed clashes, road blockades, vehicle fires and unrest in Ahome, Guamchil, Guasave and Navolato. Calling on Americans in the affected zones to remain vigilant against the risk of further violence throughout the state, the consulate advised residents to shelter in place, curtail non-essential movement and steer clear of Mexican Federal Highway 15 between Los Mochis and Culiacan. Local authorities echoed this guidance. The consulate also instructed US citizens in those municipalities to stay away from sites of law enforcement activity, remain mindful of their surroundings, steer clear of crowds and follow local media for developments, while urging them to keep relatives and friends updated on their location and safety through phone calls, text messages and social media. top_news.title: CTI writes to PM Modi, thanks him for appeal to curb gold purchases, says it saved
top_news.summary: The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, expressing gratitude for his earlier appeal to citizens to reduce gold purchases, saying his advice saved lakhs of jewellers, traders and investors from incurring heavy losses. In a letter dated November 22, CTI said the Prime Minister's advice, which had faced criticism when it was made, had helped traders avoid substantial financial losses following a decline in gold prices. Titled 'Your foresight saved lakhs of jewellers and investors from falling into debt', the letter stated that gold was priced at Rs 1.90 crore per kilogram when PM Modi advised citizens against purchasing gold, while its price has now fallen to Rs 1.25 crore per kilogram, marking a decline of Rs 65 lakh per kilogram. "If traders had ignored your advice and purchased gold at that time, they would have incurred a loss of Rs 65 lakh per kilogram today. Lakhs of jewellers would have fallen into debt and faced bankruptcy," the letter stated. Highlighting the impact of the price decline on the jewellery sector, CTI said lakhs of jewellery traders across the country maintain stocks worth several months and could have suffered losses worth crores had they purchased inventory at the earlier prices. "Lakhs of jewellery traders across the country maintain stock worth several months. Had they purchased their stock when gold was priced at Rs 1.90 crore per kilogram, they would have suffered losses worth crores today," it said. The organisation also said small traders dealing in gold through online and offline platforms, along with stock market investors, had been protected from potential losses. "Messages are continuously pouring into CTI's groups saying, 'Modi Ji has saved us'," the letter stated. CTI further claimed that even traders and jewellers who had earlier opposed the Prime Minister's advice were now acknowledging that his suggestion had been beneficial. articles.title: CTI writes to PM Modi, thanks him for appeal to curb gold purchases, says it saved
articles.summary: The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, expressing gratitude for his earlier appeal to citizens to reduce gold purchases, saying his advice saved lakhs of jewellers, traders and investors from incurring heavy losses. In a letter dated November 22, CTI said the Prime Minister's advice, which had faced criticism when it was made, had helped traders avoid substantial financial losses following a decline in gold prices. Titled 'Your foresight saved lakhs of jewellers and investors from falling into debt', the letter stated that gold was priced at Rs 1.90 crore per kilogram when PM Modi advised citizens against purchasing gold, while its price has now fallen to Rs 1.25 crore per kilogram, marking a decline of Rs 65 lakh per kilogram. "If traders had ignored your advice and purchased gold at that time, they would have incurred a loss of Rs 65 lakh per kilogram today. Lakhs of jewellers would have fallen into debt and faced bankruptcy," the letter stated. Highlighting the impact of the price decline on the jewellery sector, CTI said lakhs of jewellery traders across the country maintain stocks worth several months and could have suffered losses worth crores had they purchased inventory at the earlier prices. "Lakhs of jewellery traders across the country maintain stock worth several months. Had they purchased their stock when gold was priced at Rs 1.90 crore per kilogram, they would have suffered losses worth crores today," it said. The organisation also said small traders dealing in gold through online and offline platforms, along with stock market investors, had been protected from potential losses. "Messages are continuously pouring into CTI's groups saying, 'Modi Ji has saved us'," the letter stated.
